      <title>Kongen fullførte maraton på tiden 4.43.01</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/kongen-fullforte-maraton-pa-tiden-4.43.01-1.18076803</link>
      <description>Kongen og kronprinsessen er deltakere i French Riviera Marathon, i Nice sør i Frankrike.
Kong Haakon løp i mål på tiden 4.43.01, ifølge sporingstjenesten Trackanza.
Det var TV 2 som meldte saken først.
Et bilde viser kongen og kronprinsessen løpende ved siden av hverandre under maratonet. I maratonet er kronprinsessen registrert som Ingrid Alexandra og kongen som Haakon Magnus.
Startskuddet gikk klokka 09.16, og distansen er helmaraton på 42,125 kilometer. Løypen går langs den franske rivieraen fra Nice til Cannes.
Lørdag formiddag opplyste Slottet på nettsidene sine at «statsrådet forestår bestyrelsen av riket».
Ifølge nettsidene var kongen og kronprinsessen på privat opphold i utlandet. Det betyr at regjeringen har ansvaret for å styre og forvalte landet.
(NTB/NRK)</description>

    <item>
      <title>Ny norsk gulltriumf i VM i skyting</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/ny-norsk-gulltriumf-i-vm-i-skyting-1.18076796</link>
      <description>Caroline Finnestad Lund, Jeanette Hegg Duestad og Synnøve Berg tok laggullet på 50 meter rifle match i VM i skyting i Doha søndag.
Det var Lunds andre gull i mesterskapet. Lørdag ble 21-åringen verdensmester på 50 meter 60 skudd liggende.
Norge sanket totalt 1764 poeng under lagkonkurransen, og de kom 3,0 poeng foran Sveits på 2.-plass. Tsjekkia stakk av med bronsemedaljen. De var to poeng bak sveitserne igjen.
I eliminasjonen for lag 1 ble Finnestad Lund nummer fire med 588 poeng. Synnøve Berg ble nummer sju med 586 poeng. Duestad ble nummer tre med 590 poeng i lag 2.
Alle de tre norske jentene er videre til kvalifiseringen i den individuelle konkurransen i den samme øvelsen mandag. (NTB)</description>

    <item>
      <title>Flere skadet etter kraftig jordskjelv sentralt i Japan</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/flere-skadet-etter-kraftig-jordskjelv-sentralt-i-japan-1.18076688</link>
      <description>Minst 22 personer ble skadet da et jordskjelv med styrke 5,5 rammet Shizuoka-prefekturet i det sentrale Japan. Butikkvinduer ble knust, og folk rømte ut av bygninger.
Ifølge kringkasteren NHK er det ikke fare for tsunamier.
Skjelvet inntraff rundt klokka 1 natt til søndag. Det hadde en dybde på 41 kilometer. Den foreløpige målingen fra Japans meteorologiske institutt, som har ansvaret for overvåking og varsling av jordskjelv, var på 5,7.
Det amerikanske jordskjelvsenteret USGS målte det til 5,5.
I naboprefekturet Aichi ble det målt kraftige rystelser på nivå 5+ på den japanske skalaen – det sterkeste som er registrert der siden 1997.
(NTB)</description>

      <title>Eisenkot får i oppdrag å danne regjering i Israel</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/eisenkot-far-i-oppdrag-a-danne-regjering-i-israel-1.18076617</link>
      <description>Israels president har gitt opposisjonsleder Gadi Eisenkot i oppdrag å prøve danne regjering.
Hverken partiene som støtter statsminister Benjamin Netanyahu eller partiene som støtter Eisenkot fikk flertall ved valget 27. november.
Netanyahus blokk fikk 53 plasser i Knesset, mens blokken til Eisenkot fikk 48 mandater.
For å få flertall og bli statsminister trenger man 61 plasser i nasjonalforsamlingen. Begge blokkene er avhengig av de 19 mandatene fra de palestinsk-arabiske partiene, mend både Netanyahu og Eisenkot har sagt de ikke vil forhandle med dem.</description>

      <description>Casper Ruud har storspilt i Paris denne uken. Nå er han klar for semifinale etter seier over Nuno Borges.
Ruuds oppgjør mot portugiseren endte med 7-6 (7-5), 6-4. De to møttes for bare ni dager siden i Basel, og da snudde Borges kampen til seier.
Ruud og Borges kom til semifinalen proppfulle av selvtillit: Ingen har tapt ett sett på veien, og de hadde heller ikke gitt fra seg mer enn fire game i noen av settene.
Ruud spilte kvartfinale i Paris Masters for andre gang. For Borges, som står med én tittel i karrieren (ATP250), var dette første kvartfinale på Masters- eller Grand Slam-nivå.</description>

      <description>Thomas Markle ble pågrepet av føderale agenter i nærheten av Tampa i Florida fredag morgen amerikansk tid.

    <item>
      <title>NFF innfører semiautomatisert offside i Eliteserien</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/nff-innforer-semiautomatisert-offside-i-eliteserien-1.18075445</link>
      <description>Det opplyser Fotballforbundet på en pressekonferanse fredag.
– Prisen har kommet ned til et nivå som gjør at muligheten er der, sier generalsekretær Karl-Petter Løken.
Han opplyser at innføringen vil skje i tråd med et dommerløft. NFF bevilger 5,5 millioner kroner i 2027 til dommerløftet, og 3,5 millioner av dem skal få til semiautomatisert offside.
NFF ønsker å øke dette til 7,5 millioner kroner i 2028, og gradvis trappe opp mot 2030.
– Det du har sett med disse linjene blir borte og du får disse visningene med menneskekropper hvor du ser helt tydelig at det er offside. Det er semiautomatisert offside. Det er det ene løftet, sier Løken og fortsetter:
– Det er en utgift som tas én gang og som vil følge oss, og så vil vi trappe opp resten av investeringen i dommerutviklingene i de andre tiltakene i tillegg. Så det blir en gradvis opptrapping, eksempelvis profesjonalisering. Vi starter stille og rolig og så blir det flere og flere.
Dette skjer etter et VAR-oppgjør blant flere toppklubber. Roenborg satt ned et eget utvalg som konkluderte med at «Dagens VAR fungerer for dårlig under norske forhold. De lovte forbedringene har ikke løst hovedutfordringene, og kostnadene er for høye i forhold til kvaliteten».
Utvalget til Rosenborg stilte seg også tvilende til at semiautomatisert offside ville hjelpe VAR i norsk fotball.
– Så det vil være penger ut av vinduet hvis tinget sier nei (til VAR)? spør NRK.
– Vi kommer ikke til å diskutere detaljer i den avtalen, svarer Klaveness.</description>
      <category>Sportsnyheter</category>
      <category>Eliteserien 2026</category>

      <description>– For at folk som kunne ha de samme mulighetene til å reise som før og kunne komme seg rundt uten å bruke bilen, så øker vi antallet elsykler, sier byrådsleder Eirik Lae Solberg (H) til VG.
Det totale taket for elektriske utleiekjøretøy forblir på 16.000, men antallet elsparkesykler kuttes fra 16.000 til maksimalt 12.000. De resterende 4000 plassene settes av til elsykler når byrådet nå lyser ut ny anbudskonkurranse.
Byrådet setter også en fast nedre aldersgrense på 16 år for både elsykler og elsparkesykler.

CHEK https://cheknews.ca/ Independent and employee owned - local news stories, weather, sports, events and more Sun, 08 Nov 2026 14:00:00 +0000 en-CA hourly 1 https://cheknews.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/cropped-CHEK-Mark-512x512-1-200x200.png?crop=1 CHEK https://cheknews.ca/ 32 32 70014466 Q&A: Cumberland Community Forest Society embarks on its largest conservation project yet https://cheknews.ca/qa-cumberland-community-forest-society-embarks-on-its-largest-conservation-project-yet-1359710/ Sun, 08 Nov 2026 14:00:00 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1359710

Last month, Cumberland Community Forest Society announced the completion of a purchase of 105 hectares of forest in Cumberland known as Middle Earth.

The post Q&A: Cumberland Community Forest Society embarks on its largest conservation project yet appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Last month, Cumberland Community Forest Society announced the completion of a purchase of 105 hectares of forest in Cumberland known as Middle Earth.

Acquired from Manulife Resource Management, the $2.1 million purchase marks the organization’s largest conservation project to date, according to its website. The land is within the Trent River watershed and features popular trails used for mountain biking, hiking and trail running.

Cumberland Community Forest Society fundraises and purchases parcels of the forested areas surrounding the Village of Cumberland for conservation.

Formed in 2000 by a group of friends, the organization aims to protect these areas of forests for “ecological, historical, economic and recreational values,” according to its website. Money is raised through its trivia nights, organized fundraising events and trail runs such as The Cumby and Perseverance, as well as its monthly donors.

In an email to The Discourse, Cumberland Community Forest Society’s executive director Meaghan Cursons said much of the support for this fundraising was thanks to Cumberland resident Martha Johanson, who died in 2021 and chose to leave her home to the forest society to sell. Cursons said the sale of her home was a big part of the money raised for Middle Earth.

“The rest of the community then jumped in for some incredible fundraising over the past 18 months,” Cursons said, adding that the trail races and trivia events also played a big role.

“We are also very grateful for our generous monthly and one-time donors and for the support of the Courtenay and District Fish and Game Club, the BC Parks Foundation and the Sitka Foundation.”

Discourse reporter Madeline Dunnett reached out to Cursons via email with questions about why this project is exciting for her and what is next for the forest society. Here’s what she had to say.

The responses have been lightly edited for grammar and concision.

Madeline Dunnett: Many Comox Valley residents bike, run and walk throughout these trails. Which area of the Cumberland Forest is this? What else is special about this section of forest?

Meaghan Cursons: This area of private forest land is to the east of the existing Cumberland Forest. It includes trails like Rapture Access, SapSucker, Bonestorm, Resurrection, 2 Flats, Outfox and Round Out. This parcel stretches south right up to the base of Nikkei Mountain and includes a long wetland corridor that flows into the Trent River.

It is home to species at risk like red-legged frogs, little brown bats and painted turtles. It is an important part of the low-impact recreation network and also has important ecological values.

This is Cumberland Community Forest Society’s largest purchase to date. Can you share a bit about what the society had to undertake for a purchase this big?

The Cumberland Community Forest Society has been acquiring private forest lands for over 20 years, and we’re excited to be building on our capacity to purchase lands at this scale.

Ultimately — thanks to the E&N Land grant 140 years ago — we live in a private managed forest landscape governed under the Private Managed Forest Lands Act. The owners and manager of the lands are operating with the rules of that legislation. The likelihood of that legislation changing is low because it represents a very small per cent of the forests of the province, but a large per cent of Vancouver island.

We become aware of certain areas and become attached to their beauty only because we have recreational access to these lands through hard won agreements negotiated between private timber and the local trails community. At the same time, Cumberland Community Forest Society has been working away to acquire lands to manage for a different set of values — ecosystem health and watershed security, as well as low-impact community access — and to advocate for watershed security locally and across B.C. That’s our approach, to be open and transparent that we have different values, maintain respectful working relationships in our community and to seek opportunities to protect or purchase lands. We will continue to do that.

You purchased these [105 hectares] from Manulife Resource Management. Was this different from other purchases you made in the past? If so, how?

Our previous five purchases have all been from Manulife Resource Management. They have been an excellent partner to work with over the past 20 years and we look forward to continuing to work with them in the future. They are one of two owners in our watershed, the other being Mosaic. We also work with Mosaic on a project called the Perseverance Watershed Initiative that we hope will lead to lands being protected higher up in our drinking watershed.

Can you share a bit about how the purchase helps protect the forest? Are these areas of forest still at risk of being logged in the future at all?

The forests and watersheds of eastern Vancouver Island are all part of the E&N Land Grant legacy and the majority of the lands are still working forests. We believe that it is critically important to move significant parts of these forests out of industrial forest activity and into community ownership to allow them to recover ecologically and hydrologically. This is the core of our work.

Cumberland Community Forest Society is no stranger to setting big goals — what’s next?

We are seeking opportunities to collaborate with local government and conservation partners to expand the network of protected areas in our region.

As risk of wildfire grows year after year, we are very focused on projects that help to keep water on the landscape. We are also wanting to continue to connect areas of conservation land in the Perseverance, Trent and broader Comox Lake watersheds. We are stitching together a highly altered landscape and doing it in collaboration with our diverse community. It is such an honour to be engaged in this work.

]]> 1359710 Aid sector calls out lack of any mention of foreign aid in federal budget https://cheknews.ca/aid-sector-calls-out-lack-of-any-mention-of-foreign-aid-in-federal-budget-1359969/ Sun, 08 Nov 2026 01:02:01 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1359969

Canada's aid sector is expressing dismay over the first federal budget in more than 15 years to make no mention of foreign aid, and is calling on Ottawa to outline its vision in an upcoming foreign policy review.

The post Aid sector calls out lack of any mention of foreign aid in federal budget appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Canada’s aid sector is expressing dismay over the first federal budget in more than 15 years to make no mention of foreign aid, and is calling on Ottawa to outline its vision in an upcoming foreign policy review.

“The budget is largely silent on issues of international development co-operation and humanitarian action,” said Co-operation Canada head Kate Higgins, whose coalition includes most Canadian aid groups operating abroad.

She argued this is the wrong approach “at a time when the stakes around and the world are very high.”

The budget tabled Thursday by Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government makes no mention of international assistance, foreign aid or international development.

The Canadian Press reviewed all budgets tabled since 2010 and found references to those terms in each of those documents.

Thursday’s budget mentions Ukraine only in reference to drone production. It mentions aid workers only in passing, in a section on an existing permit program for aid organizations operating in areas under the control of groups Ottawa lists as terrorist entities.

Higgins said the sector assumes Ottawa will stick with its plan announced last year to cut $2.7 billion in foreign aid over four years.

She and other advocates said they were relieved the government did not announce further cuts. She also said Ottawa should acknowledge the important role development funding plays in addressing crises abroad, such as the humanitarian plight of Palestinians in Gaza and the spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

“International development co-operation addresses the very challenges that the government is seeking to prioritize around defence, around stability, around diplomacy, around economic partnerships, around trade diversification, around a rules-based order that upholds democracy and human rights,” Higgins said.

She said she hopes Ottawa offers more details of its plans for “international development assistance and humanitarian action” in a foreign policy review expected later this month.

In a news conference Friday, Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand said the foreign policy update will come in “in a matter of weeks” and will include “our approach on development.”

“Rest assured, development assistance is a priority for Global Affairs Canada. It is the reason why we have come forth with humanitarian assistance for Cuba, for Lebanon, for Gaza, for Sudan, among others, this year alone,” she said on Parliament Hill.

The budget’s lack of any mention of foreign aid came just days after the United Nations’ global head of humanitarian issues, Tom Fletcher, praised Canada as a “humanitarian superpower” for the world’s most vulnerable.

“I really hope that Canada continues to hold the line,” he said four days before the budget.

Results Canada, an anti-poverty advocacy group, posted a photo Thursdayof a deflated balloon on social media shortly after the budget’s release. The group’s policy director Lindsay Sheridan said her team searched the document in vain for terms relevant to her sector.

“International assistance, foreign aid, vaccines, tuberculosis — just seeing what was in it. And then continuously nothing came up. There was nothing on famines, either. And so, we were just surprised,” she told a video conference with supporters on Thursday.

“We thought that this might be the moment where we would get a little bit more context, a little more understanding of maybe the direction we would be going.”

UNICEF Canada also expressed its disappointment in the budget. It said in a news release Ottawa should at least mention international development when it talks about its response to global threats and volatility.

“International assistance helps children survive and thrive while strengthening the health, education and protection systems on which peaceful, stable societies depend,” the group wrote.

The One Campaign, which advocates for African partnerships, says Ottawa should commit to spending $5.5 billion on development annually in the interest of “safeguarding global health and humanitarian investments that underpin long-term economic stability.”

The group also wrote in a news release that Ottawa should align its “development, trade and investment institutions to support co-ordinated, mutually beneficial partnerships with African countries.”

The House of Commons finance committee had urged Ottawa to use the budget to provide more transparency on where Canada’s aid dollars are going, and to focus funding on the world’s most vulnerable.

Critics have argued the Carney government should outline clearer priorities in aid spending, and spearhead initiatives with peer countries.

Sheridan cited the Harper government’s focus on maternal health and the Trudeau government’s work on providing education to children in conflict zones. Canada led both initiatives with support from G7 peers and global financing institutions.

“It seems like a missed opportunity to make a really well-rounded, robust strategy,” she said. “It seems confusing. Not even a mention.”

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 7, 2026

Reactions to the federal government’s budget promise to end homelessness in the next 10 years are coming in as officials announce how this will happen.

On Thursday, Mark Carney’s government released the 2026 budget, offering $11.2 billion to tackle homelessness over four years, starting next year, and $17.8 billion over 10 years.

Stephanie McLean, Secretary of State (Seniors), spoke in Victoria on Saturday about the promise, saying about 65,000 people across the country are without a home.

Greater Victoria’s 2025 Point-in-Time Homeless Count estimated the region’s population of unhoused people at more than 1,700.

“That’s an astonishing number when you think of the size of our community,” McLean said.

Ottawa’s plan targets homelessness prevention, expanding access to housing and funding new mental health infrastructure.

Victoria Mayor Marianne Alto says the federal government’s plan to end homelessness is absolutely possible “with the right resources being invested by both the federal and provincial governments, and with he right collaboration with municipalities.”

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

On Friday, Alto pointed to the city’s Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan, which aims to transition people off the streets through shelters and supportive housing and into independent housing, as a model Ottawa should consider.

“That’s the type of program that we hope will be included in this federal funding and with the support of the province, and if that’s the case then we know that there will be success because we’ve already proven it.”

Mclean says Ottawa’s plan, backed by nearly $30 billion, is an unprecedented federal initiative to tackle homelessness.

The budget promises:

  • $6.5 billion to renew and strengthen the Reaching Home Initiative and support for veteran homelessness.
  • $5.5 billion to renew the Canada Housing Benefit to provide direct monthly rental assistance to low-income Canadians, including survivors of gender-based violence.
  • $5 billion for a new Integrated Supports Fund, delivered through Build Canada Homes, to build facilities that bring together housing, health care, mental health and addictions treatment, and other social services, with public, private, and philanthropic partners.
  • $2 billion for the Build Communities Strong Fund’s Health Infrastructure Fund to build new community mental health and addictions treatment facilities and refurbish existing ones. 
  • $10 billion through Build Canada Homes to support the delivery of about 25,000 supportive and transitional homes across Canada. 

“For example, here in British Columbia, we have partnered with the provincial government to build up to 700 supportive and transitional homes, as well as 400 affordable rental homes,” McLean said.

Mclean could not confirm how much of the federal funding will be coming to British Columbia, but says the province’s disproportionately high number of individuals experiencing homelessness could warrant additional funds.

“As the new provincial government is taking shape, these are conversations that are already happening, and we have gotten really good signals from the new provincial government that they are ready to build big with us,” she said.

Executive Director Dean Kurpjuweit of Vancouver’s Union Gospel Mission, which offers emergency shelter, transitional and supportive housing, says he’s hopeful about the federal announcement, but says it must be coupled with provincial funding in order to work.

B.C.’s new Conservative government has yet to be sworn in, meaning we are months away from finding out if the province’s budget will be in line with Ottawa.

Board game players in Greater Victoria now have an affordable way to play a variety of games without breaking the bank.

Nina Mosallae, library services librarian in downtown Victoria, says the Greater Victoria Public Library’s (GVPL) new take-home board game program launched in October and has already seen an overwhelming response.

“The response has been really great. We’ve had so many holds on our board games, like they’ve been flying off the shelves,” Mosallae told CHEK, adding “we had a lot of patrons itching to have access to board games, so I wasn’t really surprised to see how high the usage has been.”

The participating GVPL branches include the Central downtown location, Juan de Fuca, Oak Bay, Saanich Centennial and Bruce Hutchison.

“A lot of patrons and staff had been asking for a while, and we already had some in-branch games but people couldn’t take them home,” she says.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

Each branch offers the same collection of over 40 new games for players of all ages and abilities. Card-carrying members can take home up to two games at one time, for a period of up to three weeks.

Games like Ticket to Ride, Catan, Sequence, Cascadia, 7 Wonders, Wingspan, Exploding Kittens, Dominion, Pandemic and Quirkle are available.

The collection was created by library staff along with support from local board game cafe Interactivity Board Game Cafe on Yates Street, which helped GVPL staff get the program up and running.

“They gave us so many helpful recommendations,” says Mosallae, adding “our staff looked to buy a lot of things from the board game cafe just to make sure that we were support local business, so I know a lot of that was purchased through the board game cafe, so they’re really on board.”

Nat Guerra, Interactivity Board Game Cafe staff told CHEK, “We’re glad that the library is going to have a stock of options.”

It’s benefits the cafe on Yates Street on its busier days. While the cafe’s team of game experts help GVPL staff with recommendations, if the cafe is at capacity, players can now play at the library or check out a game.

“Knowing that the library has options, and if we have a wait list, the library is another place people can go,” says Guerra.

Saturday afternoon, the cafe was almost at full capacity and about to start a a wait list.

“As soon as the weather gets a little nastier, people want to be enjoying the great indoors,” said Guerra.

Both Guerra and Mosallae see the value of supporting the different operations.

“I think the board game cafe provides a different environment. We’re offering people to take these games to their home or wherever like a park, but the cafe has their own thing. They have food and milkshakes and they also have board game experts,” says Mosallae.

At the GVPL’s game program, players can take home a game for up to three weeks, allowing players to try the game a few times. There’s also an option to renew if no one else is in line.

But that is unlikely right now according to Mosallae and the GVPL’s online hold system, which shows cues from 10 to upwards of 23 people waiting to play games like Exploding Kittens and Settlers of Catan. But it’s a good problem to have she says.

“It’s definitely, our games are in high demand and it’s a great sign and I see that continuing,” says Mosallae.

While you can’t rent out the cafe’s games, you can bring your own or play from their extensive library of over 850 games. The cafe allows people to play games for as long as they want at just $8 per player. According to Guerra, the top three most popular games right now are Settlers of Catan, Hues and Cues and Wavelength.

“If people want to try games, we’re ready to help them out, and we’re happy to have more people playing more games” said Guerra.

With the cost of board games retailing between $50 and $100 or more, the loan program lets players explore new titles or revisit old favourites without buying them outright. Mosallae estimates the GVPL invested between $5,000 to $7,000 on the program.

“It’s just different to be able to take it home and play with your friends or family, or learn a new game in your own comfort, and a big reason we decided was because there was just demand for that,” says Mosallae.

In general, Mosallae sees nothing but positive outcomes with the new program, from building stronger social networks, learning new skills, reducing social anxiety and just having fun.

“I would say personally I’ve seen higher rates of isolation and attitudes towards isolation that maybe make us more hesitant to talk to one another.”

“So board games are just fun, it assists with helping people relax and improving your mood because when you have un you usually end up laughing and talking to people and feeling really good about yourself and your connection that you’ve made and that just makes you feel better.”

This time of year she says it’s also timely to launch, the fall and winter.

“Instead of isolating we can enjoy some cozy times playing board games with friends or family, or people we’re getting to know more. I think there’s a lot of possibility from having something as simple as board games available for people.”

The GVPL is also accepting previously owned board games donated by the public, as long as they are in good condition. Just make sure those games – and the new library games – are returned with all the pieces, says the GVPL.

“When you’re ready to pass the fun on to the next player, please make sure all pieces are included and return games directly to a service desk rather than through a book return chute,” says the GVPL’s online update.

Not to be mistaken for a violin, a talented viola player is celebrating joining the Victoria Symphony after a decade on the substitute list.

Jessica Pickersgill was born and raised in Victoria and started playing the violin when she was six. 

“They always wanted me to learn an instrument, so I think it was fun, but for longer than I care to admit, I did not enjoy it,” said Jessica with a laugh.

She switched to the viola in high school and started to think about her future.

“It was around Grade 11 when I realized, ‘Oh, I don’t know what else I’m good at, but I can do this.’ And the rest is history, as they say,” said Jessica.

She studied and played around the world, then returned home in 2016, where she started freelancing. 

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

Violinist Kathryn Weibe has been playing with Jessica for years.

“The way she plays her instrument, the way she performs with other people, the sound she makes, her musicality – but also she’s one of the most humble people I’ve ever met,” said Kathryn.

They are both passionate core members of the group Cascadia Strings. Their music and their close friendship are a perfect harmony.

“Making music is so intimate; to have that friendship alongside is just something I will always value and treasure,” said Kathryn.

It’s not easy being a professional musician, and Cascadia is just one of the jobs Jessica’s done to establish herself and make a living, including earning a spot on the sub list for the Victoria Symphony.

She’s been playing with the symphony on and off for 10 years. But she’s not a sub this season.

For the first time in 25 years, a permanent spot in the viola section opened up, and Jessica auditioned. 

“[It was] a very magical moment that I will not forget for the rest of my life,” she said.

It’s a unique and rare accomplishment that she’s extremely grateful for.

“It’s pretty magic. It’s an interesting thing because now my name’s in the program and I have a much more secure feeling, but it’s my home orchestra, and these are my colleagues and my friends,” she said.

“It’s nothing scary, it’s nothing intense, it’s more that this is where I’m meant to be.”

Former prime minister Justin Trudeau has joined England’s Oxford University in a new role.

From 2015 to 2025, Trudeau served as Canada’s prime minister before stepping down.   

The Blavatnik school, founded in 2010, says it is focused on public policy education and inspiring students to improve the “quality of government and public policy-making worldwide.”

Trudeau says in the news release that he is looking forward to “contributing his experience” and working with other leaders to “consider how governments can respond to change and build a more hopeful, inclusive and prosperous future for everyone.” 

“In the decade that I was prime minister, the world went through profound change both geopolitically and technologically, which fundamentally reshaped our world,” Trudeau said.  

Blavatnik School dean Ngaire Woods said Trudeau brings “a wealth of experience, forged through a decade of public service” which will be beneficial to students.  

“Our students are the public leaders of tomorrow, and the opportunity to learn directly from those who have navigated the complexities of government … is invaluable,” Woods said in the release.   

Trudeau is expected to visit the school later this month.
